evals.name: single-town-forecast
evals.prompt: what's the weather doing in new plymouth for the next few days? thinking of heading to the coast this weekend
evals.expected_output: Skill runs `forecast "new plymouth"` (a multi-day forecast, default 5 days), reports the forecast word, min/max and the full forecast sentence per day, and — because a coast trip is travel and the forecast mentions wind — flags any Windy / Wind rain days and checks metservice.com/warnings/home for active watches.

assertions.text: Uses scripts/metservice.py forecast for New Plymouth (not web search or a global model)
Reports per-day forecast word + min/max + the full forecast sentence (which carries the wind), not just the temperature
Because it's a travel/coast question mentioning the weekend, flags wind (Windy / Wind rain words) and mentions checking MetService warnings
Quotes the issued time or otherwise conveys currency

evals.name: best-town-comparison
evals.prompt: which of tauranga, hamilton, rotorua or napier is the best bet for a fine warm weekend? want somewhere dry
evals.expected_output: Skill runs `compare tauranga hamilton rotorua napier`, then does NOT just pick the warmest/sunniest cell — it sanity-checks the leading town's full forecast sentence for wind or fog before declaring a winner, and notes that Windy / Wind rain words flag possible gale conditions.

assertions.text: Uses the compare subcommand across all four towns
Does not rank on a single metric — checks the winner's full forecast text for wind/fog before recommending it
Explicitly caveats confidence beyond ~5 days if the horizon is that far out, or flags wind where present

evals.name: current-conditions
evals.prompt: how cold is it in taupō right now and is it raining?
evals.expected_output: Skill runs `obs "Taupō"` (macron handled by slugify), reporting current temp, wind chill, and rain last 3h/24h, with the observation time for currency.

assertions.text: Uses the obs subcommand for current conditions (not a multi-day forecast)
Passes the macronised name through — relies on the script's macron stripping rather than failing or asking the user to re-spell it
Reports temperature and recent rainfall, and the observation time

evals.name: hourly-wind-for-activity
evals.prompt: planning to fly my drone in wellington this afternoon — what are the gusts looking like hour by hour?
evals.expected_output: Skill runs `hourly wellington`, surfacing the per-hour wind and especially the gust column, and notes that Wellington gusts can flag a wind watch worth checking at metservice.com/warnings/home.

assertions.text: Uses the hourly subcommand (the only one carrying gust data)
Highlights gust speeds specifically, not just average wind
Mentions checking MetService warnings if gusts are high
